TLDR: Cache entiredb-cluster→entire-core mappings

#  Problem

  Resolving which login context to use for an `entire://` cluster mixed two concerns: which control plane fronts a cluster (stable infra) and which of your accounts to use (per-user). When several contexts were eligible and none was active, it picked one by last-save order and persisted that guess as a binding — so the choice was somewhat arbitrary, and the stored state ended up asymmetric and confusing.

#  99% happy path: unchanged

  - One account → exactly one eligible context → used automatically. No prompt, no extra step.
  - No added latency — `/.well-known` is cached; first op per cluster fetches once, as before.
  - No migration / re-login — existing `contexts.json` loads as-is; the obsolete `cluster_contexts` key is ignored and removed.
  - A new error fires only on genuine ambiguity (2+ accounts on the same core, none active) — previously a silent guess (e.g., `admin@core`, `paul@core` both match), now a clear "pick one."

#  Change

  - Cache only the objective `cluster → [core_urls]` fact (in `cluster_cores.json`, 24h TTL, stale-fallback). The matching account is recomputed locally every op, never persisted.
  - Selection: active context if eligible → else the sole eligible one → else (2+ eligible, none active) a one-line error listing them and pointing at `entire auth use`, instead of guessing.
  - Drops the now-defunct bind/unbind surface.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **High Risk**
> Changes how every `entire://` operation picks credentials (auth path); wrong selection or stale core cache could block git or use the wrong account until the user runs `entire auth use` or clears cache.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR **splits cluster auth into infra vs identity**: only **which cores front a cluster** is cached (`cluster_cores.json`, 24h TTL, stale fallback on discovery failure); **which login context to use** is recomputed every git op and never written to disk.
> 
> **`entire://` resolution** loads cores from cache or `/.well-known`, then picks a context: active context if its core is eligible → else the only eligible context → else an error listing candidates and pointing at `entire auth use` (no silent multi-account guess).
> 
> **Removed** persisted `cluster_contexts`, `BindCluster` / `File.Resolve`, and **`entire auth unbind`** plus cluster-binding output from **`entire auth contexts`**. **Logout / delete** no longer auto-advance `current_context` to another stored identity.
> 
> Shared discovery cache I/O is refactored for the new cores file; **`git-remote-entire`** passes the discovery cache dir into resolution. **`.gitignore`** adds `/git-remote-entire`.

## Review: PR #1318 — "Vastly simplify auth contexts"

### Verdict
The core change is **well-designed and solid**. Splitting "which cores front a cluster" (objective infra → cached) from "which account to use" (recomputed every op, never persisted) is the right call, and it cleanly kills the old footgun where an arbitrary same-core account got persisted as a binding. Code is well-factored, comments explain the *why*, and test coverage is genuinely good (cache hit/miss/stale-fallback, ambiguity, sole-eligible, active-wins). One thing should be fixed before merge: a batch of **user-facing help text and doc comments still describe the binding model you just removed**.

### Must fix before merge — stale "binding" narrative leaks to users
The functional removal is complete, but several user-facing strings and package docs still tell users about `cluster_contexts` bindings that no longer exist:

1. **`cmd/entire/cli/logout.go:44` and `:64`** (user-facing — `entire logout --help` / flag help):
   - `"...can still authenticate ... against clusters they are bound to. Use --all to remove every saved login and its cluster bindings."`
   - flag desc: `"Remove all saved logins (contexts) and their cluster bindings..."`
   - `RemoveAllContexts` no longer touches any bindings — they're gone. This is now factually wrong.

2. **`cmd/entire/cli/auth_context.go:14-15, 28-29, 66`** — the `newAuthUseCmd` doc comment, its `Long` help text (`"a cluster already bound to a context keeps using that binding, so switching here affects only clusters not yet bound..."`), and the **runtime** `warnIfCrossCoreContext` output (`"...a cluster already bound to another context keeps using it; the active context applies only to clusters not yet bound."`). Post-PR the active context *is* consulted for every cluster it's eligible for — there's no "not yet bound" set anymore.

3. **`cmd/git-remote-entire/main.go:15`** — package doc: `"an explicit cluster binding, else /.well-known discovery"`. Now it's always cores-cache-or-discovery.

4. **`internal/entireclient/contexts/contexts.go:8-11`** — package doc still lists `cluster_contexts` as a field and calls `current_context` "the fallback for clusters with no binding." The field is deleted.

None of these are logic bugs, but #1 and #2 ship incorrect guidance via `--help` and a live warning, so they're worth fixing in this PR rather than as a follow-up.

### Behavioral change worth a conscious confirmation (not a bug)
In `selectContext`/`eligibleContexts`, eligibility is now gathered across **all** advertised cores. Old code iterated `body.CoreURLs` and picked the first advertised core that had any local context. So for a cluster fronted by cores `[A, B]` where the user has exactly one account on `A` and one on `B` (neither active), the **old** code silently picked A's account; the **new** code returns the "ambiguous, pick one" error. That's more correct and aligned with the PR's "refuse to guess" philosophy, and multi-core-fronting is rare — just flagging that it's a real change in that edge case, not just a refactor.

### Things I checked and liked
- **`current_context` no longer auto-advances on delete/logout** (`Delete`, `RemoveCurrentContext`) — correct; silently re-authing as another identity was the more dangerous default.
- **Stale-fallback on discovery failure** is well-handled and tested; a brief cluster outage won't break ops whose cores you already knew. The stale entry's `FetchedAt` is intentionally not bumped, so it keeps trying to refresh — good.
- **`cache.go` generics refactor** (`withCacheFileLock` / `modifyCacheFile` / `loadCacheFile`) is a clean dedup; `Set` copies the slice (tested), atomic temp+rename and flock are preserved, corrupt-cache self-heal preserved.
- **Revocation immediacy is preserved**: only cores are cached (24h), account selection stays live, so `entire auth use` and context deletion still take effect on the next op.

### Minor
- `.gitignore` adds `/git-remote-entire` (built binary) — fine.

Want me to apply the doc/help-text fixes (items 1–4)? They're mechanical and I can do them in one pass.
